```{r setup, include=FALSE}
set.seed(0121)
library(igraph)
library(tidygraph)
library(ggraph)
theme_set(theme_graph()) 

library(igraphdata)
data("UKfaculty")

UK <- as_tbl_graph(UKfaculty)

UK <- UK |>
  activate(edges) |>
  filter(edge_is_mutual()) |>
  to_undirected() |>
  simplify() |>
  as_tbl_graph()
```

## Community Detection Review

- What is a component? (Hint: there's often one "giant" component)
- What is a clique?
- What is the weakness of cliques as a way of identifying groups?
- What is a k-plex? (Hint: related to cliques)

## Coreness Example

<div class='col fragment'>
```{r,message=F}
UK |>
  activate(nodes) |>
  mutate(coreness = node_coreness()) |>
ggraph(layout='stress') +
  geom_edge_fan(alpha=.3) +
  geom_node_point(aes(color=coreness)) +
  scale_color_viridis_c(name='Coreness')
```

## Discussion Questions

- How should we think about departure in social networks. E.g., could changes in community membership make a group appear more radical even if individual members' opinions have not changed?
- When looking at a workplace, employees are in different departments, but many people still know each other and build relationships outside of their departments. How can a network have strong communities while still being connected as a whole? 

## Discussion Questions

- Do you think social movements are more successful because of a small group of highly influential people or because of the large number of less active people spreading information?
- How do researchers decide where one community ends and another begins when someone is connected to multiple different groups?

## Discussion Questions
- How can organizers or these core participants encourage people on the periphery to become more involved without actually requiring them to have the same level of commitment as people in the core? With that being said, is there a line to be drawn where asking too much of the periphery will actually result in them doing less?
- How is k-core decomposition different from Girvan and Newman's betweenness method?
- Would the findings from the Barbera et al. paper still hold today now that algorithms decide what you see instead of who you follow?
